examples.purpose: A settings card, the guide's In context: a Card holding three rows, each a horizontal ListItem whose title names the setting, with no support text and no arrow, and a Toggle at its end named with the same words. Each change applies as soon as the toggle moves; the screen keeps the values and saves them. The literal values and the empty onValueChange stand for the screen's own state and saving.
examples.jsx:
<Card>
  <VStack>
    <ListItem
      layout="Horizontal"
      navArrow={false}
      title="Payment alerts"
      showSupportText={false}
      trailing={<Toggle value onValueChange={(value) => {}} accessibilityLabel="Payment alerts" />}
    />
    <ListItem
      layout="Horizontal"
      navArrow={false}
      title="Biometric login"
      showSupportText={false}
      trailing={<Toggle value={false} onValueChange={(value) => {}} accessibilityLabel="Biometric login" />}
    />
    <ListItem
      layout="Horizontal"
      navArrow={false}
      title="Hide balances"
      showSupportText={false}
      trailing={<Toggle value={false} onValueChange={(value) => {}} accessibilityLabel="Hide balances" />}
    />
  </VStack>
</Card>

from.quote: Each change applies as soon as the toggle moves. The screen keeps every value and saves it; the toggle only reports the new value.

props.name: value
props.description: On the web, aria-checked follows the value. Declared: Whether the toggle is on (controlled)

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value (uncontrolled) Default false, from the component source.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called once with the new value for each Enter, Space or click. Declared: Callback when the toggle state changes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: On the web, sets aria-disabled and tabindex -1, so Tab skips it. Declared: Whether the toggle is disabled. Default false, from the component source.

modes.name: Color Mode
modes.description: A token collection Toggle reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

modes.name: Toggle States
modes.description: A token collection Toggle reads (the package's FIGMA_COMPONENT_MODES). When modes leave it unset, the resolver uses the collection's default mode.

events.name: onValueChange
events.description: Callback when the toggle state changes

gaps.text: Figma has two variants, Off and On, both 52 × 31; disabled exists only in the package, which dims the toggle to 50% and greys the track in both states.
Disabled On and Disabled Off share one grey track, so only the thumb position shows the state.
